Consult Summary:
- Adult with known atopic asthma presents with 2–3 days of wheeze, exertional dyspnea, and dry cough; exam not performed (teleconsult). Clinician impression: asthma exacerbation likely triggered by allergens or viral illness; plan includes increased SABA via spacer, peak flow monitoring, antihistamine, and 1-week review.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Wheezing and shortness of breath.
- Timeline:
  - Onset 2–3 days ago; acute.
  - Symptoms worsen with walking/exertion; currently feels well at rest.
  - Sometimes has difficulty completing sentences during episodes.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Dry cough.
  - Felt “feverish,” but measured temperature 37°C.
  - No chest pain.
  - No sputum production.
  - No hemoptysis.
  - Not woken from sleep by symptoms.
  - Unable to walk to work due to breathlessness; can climb stairs.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Worse with exertion.
  - No home peak flow meter.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No smoking.
  - No nighttime awakenings.
  - No chest pain, no hemoptysis.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma: Childhood onset; “quite bad,” required inhalers; occasional hospital visits (no ICU), occasional missed school. Stopped regular medications a few years ago; currently uses salbutamol intermittently.
- Atopy: Hay fever and eczema.

Medications:
- Salbutamol inhaler PRN (reports use every few weeks and with exercise); dose/route/frequency not documented.
- No other regular medications reported.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: Approximately one glass of wine every 2–3 days.
- Lives with partner.
- Occupation: Engineer. Currently working from home or on sick leave due to symptoms. Normally walks to work but cannot currently due to dyspnea.

Family History:
- Not mentioned.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Patient-reported temperature 37°C.
- Examination findings: Not recorded.

Investigations:
- None performed during consult.
- Orders/arrangements:
  - Peak flow meter prescribed; patient to record readings morning and evening for 1 week.
  - Spacer prescribed; pharmacist to demonstrate use.

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - Likely asthma exacerbation in an atopic adult with recent 2–3 days of wheeze and exertional dyspnea, potentially triggered by allergens or a viral illness. Currently stable at rest.

- DDx Integration (brief):
  - Asthma exacerbation (allergic/viral trigger) — supports: atopic history, prior asthma, acute wheeze and exertional dyspnea; opposes: no nocturnal symptoms.
  - Viral URI/acute bronchitis with bronchospasm — supports: short duration, dry cough; opposes: afebrile by measurement, no URI features reported.
  - COVID-19 precipitating asthma — supports: cough/dyspnea; opposes: no classic features/exposures documented, measured temp normal.

- Issue 1: Acute asthma exacerbation
  - Plan:
    - Increase salbutamol use: take 2–4 puffs every 4 hours initially via spacer (as advised).
    - Prescribe spacer; pharmacist to teach correct inhaler technique.
    - Prescribe peak flow meter and record values AM and PM for the next week.
    - Safety-net: If a high temperature develops or wheeze worsens, call back immediately for further advice.
    - Follow-up: Arrange asthma review in about 1 week to assess control and review peak flow diary; may consider additional/controller medication at that time.

- Issue 2: Allergic rhinitis/hay fever (possible trigger)
  - Plan:
    - Start a regular over-the-counter antihistamine (pharmacist guidance; clinician to note recommendation in records).

- Issue 3: Functional limitation due to respiratory symptoms
  - Plan:
    - Continue working from home as needed until symptoms improve; reassess activity tolerance at follow-up.

General plan items if applicable:
- None beyond the above.

Quality checks:
- Missing but expected: Objective vitals (HR, RR, SpO2), physical exam findings, current medication doses/frequency, personal best peak flow, COVID exposure/testing, immunization status, formal asthma action plan.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None material. Patient felt “feverish” but measured 37°C (not febrile).
- Transcript quality: Some unclear responses regarding past inhaler use, but clarified that patient uses salbutamol intermittently; otherwise adequate history for remote consult.
